1.why: Modifier item: C is the only option with an active human agent as subject; A/D are passives and B is an expletive, the standard dangling-modifier distractor cast.

2.why: Possessive/contraction set: the key must be a possessive (their/its), and I bet singular 'its' because the usual trap is a collective antecedent pulling students to 'their'.

3.why: Complement set: 'to satisfy' is the lone infinitive against two gerund forms and a full clause, and the infinitive is the unmarked complement.

4.why: Agreement set: 'requires' is the lone singular against three plural-agreeing forms (lone-number bet).

5.why: Modifier item: three options concern the mural, so the modifier describes the mural; C names the mural itself while D substitutes its possessive ('the mural's colors') and B an expletive.

6.why: Tense set: 'fought' is the lone simple/unmarked form against two perfects and a progressive (unmarked-tense bet).

7.why: Tense set: 'cleared' is the lone simple form against future-perfect, past-perfect and conditional-perfect lures.

8.why: Agreement set: 'is' is the lone singular against were/have been/are (lone-number bet).

9.why: Agreement set: 'are' is the lone plural against has been/was/is (lone-number bet, applied in the same direction as item 8).

10.why: Agreement set: 'were' is the lone plural against has been/was/is.

11.why: Mark set {comma, colon, semicolon, ' that is'}: the comma is the splice lure and the bare connective the fragment lure; I bet the colon over the semicolon because the co-present ' that is' implies an explanatory restatement rather than a second independent clause.

12.why: Tense set: 'collected' is the lone simple form against a conditional, a bare participle and a past-perfect progressive.

13.why: Boundary set: bare 'they'/'it' would splice after a comma, leaving 'which' and 'and it'; I bet the relative, which is the more commonly keyed of the two.

14.why: Pronoun set: 'they' is the lone plural against one/you/he (same lone-number bet as the agreement items).

15.why: Only the mark varies before 'are': a colon or semicolon cannot precede a bare verb and a comma cannot split subject from verb, so the no-mark option is the only legal one.

16.why: ', but' is the only conventional coordination; ', ' alone splices, '; but' is redundant, and ' but,' strands the comma after the conjunction.

17.why: Tense set with no lone aspect; defaulting to the simple present as the unmarked form for a general statement.

18.why: Agreement set: 'is' is the lone singular against were/are/have been.

19.why: Possessive set: 'it's' and 'there' are the homophone lures, and I bet singular 'its' over 'their' for the same collective-antecedent reason as item 2.

20.why: Modifier set: C is absurd (unrolling the archaeologist) and D dangles with no object; A is the only option that supplies its own agent explicitly rather than depending on a forward pronoun as B does.

21.why: 'being' and '; and' are the two dead distractors; with 'flour' opening what reads as a list after a complete clause the colon is the key and the comma the lure.

22.why: 'nurses's' is never legal; three of four forms are built on the plural noun, so I bet the plural possessive over the singular possessive.

23.why: Agreement set: 'is' is the lone singular against have been/were/are.

24.why: Modifier item: C is the only option whose subject is the named person, the required agent for an introductory participle about Dr. Halloran; A/B shift the subject and D is an expletive.
